design_gotchas.title: Push-Pull Output — Do NOT Wired-AND or Pull Up to a Different Logic Rail
design_gotchas.detail: TLV3201AIDBVR features an active push-pull CMOS output (driving up to 60 mA sourcing / 48 mA sinking at 5 V)—NOT an open-drain or open-collector output like LM393DR or LMV7235. Tying multiple outputs together in a wired-AND fault bus or pulling OUT up to a higher/lower voltage domain causes direct rail-to-rail bus contention and destructive shoot-through current.

design_gotchas.title: Identical SOT-23-5 Pinout to Single Op-Amps (TLV9001/TLV9061/OPA333) — Incompatible With LMV321IDBVR
design_gotchas.detail: TLV3201AIDBVR (1=OUT, 2=GND, 3=IN+, 4=IN-, 5=VCC) matches the exact SOT-23-5 DBV pinout of linear op-amps TLV9001IDBVR, TLV9061IDBVR, and OPA333AIDBVR, but is an uncompensated 43 ns high-speed comparator that oscillates violently in linear negative-feedback op-amp sockets. Conversely, its pins 1/3/4 are permuted relative to LMV321IDBVR (1=IN+, 3=IN-, 4=OUT).

design_gotchas.title: Fast 2.9 ns / 3.7 ns Edges and Push-Pull Switching Shoot-Through Require Local 0.1 µF Decoupling
design_gotchas.detail: With 2.9 ns rise / 3.7 ns fall times and 1.2 mV typical internal hysteresis, fast push-pull output transitions create brief VCC-to-GND shoot-through current pulses (Section 8.1.3). Place a low-ESR 0.1 µF ceramic capacitor directly across pins 2 and 5 and add external positive-feedback hysteresis for slowly varying or noisy inputs to avoid output chatter.

design_gotchas.title: Back-to-Back Input ESD Clamp Network Limits Differential Overdrive Above Supply
design_gotchas.detail: Although common-mode range extends 200 mV beyond both rails without phase inversion, Section 8.1.1 (Figure 8-2) shows internal back-to-back input clamp diodes with 1 kΩ resistors. Avoid differential input voltages exceeding VCC and limit over-rail input current to ≤10 mA using external series resistors.

typical_use_cases: High-speed 2.7 V–5.5 V PWM current-limit protection, pulse-width monitoring, and fault detectors
Battery-powered zero-crossing detectors and threshold triggers requiring 43 ns speed at 40 µA Iq
Optical receiver, time-of-flight, and high-speed sampling clock/edge slicing on 3.3 V/5 V rails
Direct CMOS/TTL logic-level Schmitt triggers without external pull-up resistors
engineering_summary: The Texas Instruments TLV3201AIDBVR is an ultra-low-power (40 µA typ), high-speed (43 ns typ propagation delay at 5 V / 100 mV overdrive; 40 ns headline) single rail-to-rail input comparator with an active push-pull CMOS output in a 5-pin SOT-23 (DBV) package operating from 2.7 V to 5.5 V (-40°C to +125°C). Featuring 1 pA input bias current, 3 mV max offset, 1.2 mV internal hysteresis, and input common-mode range 200 mV beyond both rails without phase inversion, it eliminates pull-up resistors while demanding caution against wired-AND bus contention and op-amp socket confusion on the identical TLV9001/TLV9061/OPA333 SOT-23-5 footprint.

audit_notes: Visually verified TLV3201 DBV (SOT-23-5) Top View pinout on 300 DPI PNG page 3 (Figure 5-1 & Pin Functions table): 1=OUT, 2=GND, 3=IN+, 4=IN-, 5=VCC (identical to TLV9001/TLV9061/OPA333 DBV op-amps; reversed pins 1/3/4 vs LMV321IDBVR).
Verified push-pull output architecture, Abs Max (7 V, TJ=150°C), Recommended Operating (2.7 V–5.5 V), and TLV3201 DBV RθJA = 237.8 °C/W, RθJC(top) = 108.7 °C/W on page 4 PNG.

Verified Section 6.5/6.6 (5 V) and 6.7/6.8 (2.7 V) on pages 5-6 PNGs: VIO-TLV3201 = 3 mV max (distinct from TLV3202 5 mV), IB = 1 pA typ, IQ = 40 µA typ, ISC = 48 mA sink / 60 mA source, tPD = 43 ns L-to-H (42 ns H-to-L) at 5 V / 100 mV OD (47/45 ns at 20 mV OD, 50 ns max).
